Providence Health Plan  
Appeals and Grievance Department  
P.O. Box 4158  
Portland, OR 97208-4158  

Re: Internal appeal of denial of total shoulder replacement  
Member: Emerson Lawson  
Member ID: W445912797  
Reference number: POC-5717F9EEEF-88905  
Requested procedure: Total shoulder replacement  
CPT: 23472  
Date of denial notice: August 2, 2026  

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for my total shoulder replacement. The denial states that the documentation was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. The clinical records support the applicable Providence medical-necessity requirements for CPT 23472 and provide the information needed to review this request.

The Providence policy document I located is titled Total Shoulder Arthroplasty, medical policy number MP430, effective June 1, 2026, with a last review date of April 2026. The policy identifies total shoulder arthroplasty under CPT 23472 as potentially medically necessary when the stated criteria are met.

The records address those criteria as follows:

1. No active infection

The clinical summary documents no active infection of the shoulder joint.

2. Pain and functional impairment

The patient has had nine months of progressive shoulder pain that has not been relieved by rest. The pain and loss of function interfere with activities of daily living: the patient cannot reach overhead, cannot dress without assistance, and cannot sleep on the affected side.

The examination documents substantial loss of motion, with active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees and external rotation limited to 10 degrees, together with glenohumeral crepitus.

The policy states that the required pain-related findings may include:

“Pain interferes with activities of daily living (ADLs); or”

“Pain is increased with initiation of activity; or”

“Pain occurs with range of motion (ROM)”

The records clearly document pain interfering with activities of daily living and document painful shoulder disease with marked range-of-motion limitation and crepitus. If Providence believes the submitted records do not expressly state whether pain occurs with range of motion or with initiation of activity, please identify that specific deficiency and allow submission of an addendum from Duval, MD.

3. Imaging-confirmed osteoarthritis and structural disease

The May 21, 2026 shoulder radiographs show complete loss of the glenohumeral joint space, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. CT confirms an intact rotator cuff.

These findings document advanced glenohumeral osteoarthritis with the structural abnormalities addressed by the policy. The examination also documents both limited range of motion and glenohumeral crepitus.

The policy requires, for osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis, limited range of motion or crepitus with glenohumeral joint rotation, together with either bone-on-bone imaging or continued symptoms despite conservative treatment and specified structural findings. The records provide both pathways: complete loss of the glenohumeral joint space consistent with bone-on-bone end-stage arthritis, as well as continued symptoms despite conservative treatment and multiple structural findings, including osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, joint-space loss, and glenoid deformity.

4. Conservative treatment

The patient has completed eight weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening, including 20 visits from April 11, 2026, through June 6, 2026. The physical therapy discharge note documents this treatment.

The patient also used NSAIDs for six months with inadequate relief. A corticosteroid injection on March 22, 2026, provided only four weeks of partial relief. Despite these measures, the patient continues to have progressive pain and severe functional limitation.

The policy describes conservative treatment as including NSAID, acetaminophen, or corticosteroid treatment; physical therapy, occupational therapy, or home exercise; and activity modification. The submitted records document substantially more than the stated minimum duration for medication treatment and physical therapy, as well as failure of the corticosteroid injection to provide lasting relief. If documentation of activity modification is required, please identify that requirement specifically and permit the treating surgeon to provide an addendum.

5. Additional clinical information

The examination shows glenohumeral crepitus, severe restriction of motion, and intact cuff strength. CT confirms an intact rotator cuff. The patient has no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and is a non-smoker. These facts further support the appropriateness of proceeding with the requested shoulder replacement.

The submitted documentation is sufficient to evaluate medical necessity under the applicable Providence policy. At minimum, the records establish advanced osteoarthritis, severe pain and functional impairment, objective loss of motion and crepitus, failure of prolonged conservative care, and no active infection.

Please overturn the denial and approve CPT 23472. If Providence continues to find the submission incomplete, please provide a detailed written list of each missing document or clinical fact, identify the specific criterion to which it relates, and allow the requested information to be submitted before issuing a final adverse determination. Please also provide the exact clinical-review criteria used for this request, including any InterQual criteria applied.

Sincerely,

Emerson Lawson
